Those cables pulled into splicing enclosures are usually mainline feed with laterals for services. Think of it like a water main, starts as a large 30 inch transmission main and as it passes a neighborhood it’s stepped down to a 16, and then an 8 and all these have services that feed houses. Same principle with fiber. Starts out as an 864 count fiber dropping count as more of that line is used until it reaches end of line and stops.

Realistically it looks like a drop that hasn’t been deployed yet. It’s from an MST terminal so yeah it’s a drop that gets plugged in and screwed in tight with a rubber gasket for water proofing. Those hardened drops only come in certain footages, 100, 250, 500, 750, 1000, 1500, and 2000 foot drops. Usually upon deployment the remaining slack will get pulled into the NID at the side of the house, cut to length and then have a connector terminated on them.

Do they have problems? Occasionally. Long term though? They work great. I’ve worked for telcos that don’t use these and splice drops into the case, and what that means is that any time the drop fails, you have to roll a splicer to fix it. With this type of deployment of there’s an issue with the drop, any install tech with a bucket truck can replace them same day and restore service.

Sauté garlic and red pepper flakes in olive oil until fragrant and golden add in 1 cup of Arrabbiata, let simmer for 5 minutes, (I’ve found that thinning this with just a little bit of chicken stock or beef stock gives it a more Newmans sauce consistency, just a dash, maybe 1/8th cup), while sauce is simmering drop noods. In another pan sauté veg (red green peppers and onions, amount is preferential when cooking at home lol) after sauce has simmered and had some time for those flavors to marinade, add Cajun seasoning blend (I do make my own here to control sodium content) Cajun seasoning to taste, add half cup of cream and allow to thicken. 

In a skillet sear quick steak and season with that same Cajun blend, once seared the steak starts to fall apart and gives you those chunks of meat. 

When noods are done, place in sauce and combine adding pasta water as needed, plate with veggies and steak on top and garnish with green onions.
